Priya R.: Heads-up everyone — we’re rolling out a compatibility / pinning playbook for SDK consumers to handle an upcoming runtime contract change. :warning:
Mateo H.: what change exactly?
Priya R.: The SDK v4 release will stop normalizing optional kwargs (e.g., `truncate=True` -> `truncate='auto'`) and will enforce strict param names. That impacts code that relied on loose arg coercion.
Alice W.: ok, so some existing callsites could break on v4 if they relied on coercion. Do we have a migration path?
Priya R.: Yes — two tracks: 1) pin to the last v3-compatible SDK in production, 2) use the rw-compat helper (temporary shim) to opt a service into v3-compatible behavior. We published a playbook with checklists and a small interop library. :sparkles:
docs-bot: Published playbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk-compat-playbook (includes checklist, CI lint rule, and canary guide)
Jamal K.: link looks good. Can you drop the quick pin example here for folks doing an urgent hotfix?
Priya R.: sure — pip / npm examples below. Use this to pin in your requirements or package.json.

```
# python
# requirements.txt
redwood-sdk==3.12.4

# node
# package.json
"dependencies": {
  "@redwood/inference": "3.12.4"
}
```

Priya R.: For services that need to upgrade, the rw-compat shim can be added as a stopgap:

```
# python example
from redwood_compat import CompatLayer
client = CompatLayer(api_key=..., target_version="3")
# CompatLayer will coerce legacy kwargs for you for up to 90 days
```

Mateo H.: how long will we support rw-compat?
Priya R.: We plan to support the shim for 90 days after the v4 GA. The playbook has a suggested schedule: canary (2 wks) -> org-wide opt-in (4 wks) -> v4 GA and shim deprecation starts (90 days).
Alice W.: any CI linters or tests we can add to catch issues earlier?
Priya R.: yes — we added a pre-commit lint rule and pytest plugin that fail when a callsite uses deprecated/loose params. Example commands in the playbook: `pip install redwood-compat-lint` then run `redwood-compat-lint --check src/`.
Jamal K.: will console/hosted customers get automatic fallback?
Priya R.: Hosted API will accept both styles for a transitional period, but dedicated/private deploys must opt into the compatibility layer themselves. We’ll make policy notes in the admin console.
Mateo H.: any telemetry we’re collecting to estimate impact?
Priya R.: Opt-in telemetry is available; playbook includes a small eval prompt set and a SQL query for tokenized callsites so you can estimate how many functions will hit strict validation. We’re not collecting argument payloads — only shape and param-name footprints (opt-in).
Alice W.: who should eng teams ping if they hit blockers during rollout?
Priya R.: Ping me (@priya) and Mateo on #eng-runtime, or open an issue in the infra repo with label `sdk-compat`. We’ll coordinate emergency compatibility gates.
Jamal K.: noted. I’ll add the lint to our CI and run the SQL fingerprint query tomorrow.
Priya R.: TL;DR: 1) If you need zero-change: pin to 3.12.4 2) For gradual upgrades: use rw-compat shim + follow playbook 3) Add compat-lint to CI 4) Contact eng-runtime if you see failures.
docs-bot: The playbook also contains a checklist for PMs to coordinate client-facing notices and dashboard flags.
Alice W.: thanks — this is clear. Please drop the playbook PR in #docs when ready so we can review.
Priya R.: Will do. Expect the full docs + shim release tomorrow morning (UTC). :thumbsup:
